goal: Hook on a character's tired week, then the parts of wellness (physical, mental, social) and how they act on each other; ends in a choice for the character and a reason.

goal: Habits build a cause-and-effect chain across the parts of wellness (sleep and mood, activity and focus, friends and stress), built on chain cards for one character.

note: End-of-unit assessment: two or three unseen scenarios read alone or aloud on request, the steps written for the character, one facts-in-use item per unit fact, one valuing item scored on whether the reason uses a unit fact; no cards; met, partly or not yet. Sensitivity flag: body (cases are characters'; any student may take another case, and a student who wants help talks privately with the nurse or counselor).

goal: Teams carry out the habit at school and log it; at this lesson each team monitors progress and decides to keep or change the plan.
note: The habit runs in the weeks between lessons (unit 26 spans weeks 18 to 22). Teacher record of each student's part in carrying out the habit and keeping the log. Candidate kept: track a habit with a simple log (no day cost). Safety: the walking group follows the school's active-play and supervision rules, on school grounds, with water and a way for any student to take part; $12 poster paper and markers for the poster run. Logs are about the team's habit, never students' bodies. Sensitivity flag: body (cases are characters'; any student may take another case, and a student who wants help talks privately with the nurse or counselor).

goal: Second monitoring lesson: read the log, judge progress, adjust the plan.
note: Teacher record continues. A student may also keep a private personal goal from the safe list. Sensitivity flag: body (cases are characters'; any student may take another case, and a student who wants help talks privately with the nurse or counselor).

goal: Third monitoring lesson; each team writes its write-up of the habit and the changes it made.
note: The team write-up is a draft; the teacher gives written feedback before day 128. Sensitivity flag: body (cases are characters'; any student may take another case, and a student who wants help talks privately with the nurse or counselor).

goal: Examine how setting the goal affected health and well-being for the team and the school, and what to carry into the next goal; teams revise the write-up from the written feedback.
note: Scored on the steps and the student's account, never on whether the habit worked. The teacher models one effect write-up first. Sensitivity flag: body (cases are characters'; any student may take another case, and a student who wants help talks privately with the nurse or counselor).

goal: End-of-unit check: the team record and each student's monitoring sheet scored on the goal-plan steps and the student's account, with one unseen character log to judge and one unseen team scene in a different setting (a class group or a club): write what the character does to work well with the others.
note: End-of-unit assessment: two or three unseen scenarios read alone or aloud on request, the steps written for the character, one facts-in-use item per unit fact, one valuing item scored on whether the reason uses a unit fact; no cards; met, partly or not yet. The doing record (NHES.S7.8.3, NHES.S6.8.5) is the teacher's record from days 125 to 127; the teacher's day 123 to 127 record of each student's part is also scored on the teamwork steps (NHES.S4.8.7). SEL unit 18 (weeks 27 to 31) opens with the team habit as retrieval; it is not the same project. Self-check 2 after the check. Sensitivity flag: body (cases are characters'; any student may take another case, and a student who wants help talks privately with the nurse or counselor).

goal: Fitting advocacy to its audience and setting (a lunch ask to a principal, a note to families, a post for peers), with a claim, one fact with its source, and the ask.
note: Retrieval task: grade 7 speak-up plan and alone or in a group (unit 18). ELA grade 8 unit 2 (argument for an audience) comes first; its argument is used. Speak-up plan card, grade 8 form: fitted to the audience. Audiences are at school; no student posts online for the class; messages are about places and rules, never a person or a body. Home task goes out (English and Spanish): a talk with a trusted adult the student chooses; a school adult counts. HBO: FN.HBO12; PA.HBO1, HBO5, HBO7; S.HBO8.

goal: Write a short talk, flyer or invitation for a real school audience; the teacher writes feedback.
note: The counted draft day. Candidate kept: encouraging others to be active fits the audience choice. Self-check 1: each student rates their own use of the steps and names one next step (kept by the student).

goal: Revise the piece from the written feedback and practice the delivery in pairs from the speak-up card.
note: ELA grade 8 unit 5 (presentations, weeks 26 to 32) comes later: health's three-part short talk (claim, one fact with its source, the ask); a flyer or written invitation meets the indicator for a student who does not speak to an audience. $4 flyer printing.

goal: Deliver to the real audience (a class, the principal, families at a school event, a PE class).
note: Teacher record of each student's part in delivering it (the doing record). Family note for sensitive unit 28 (dating violence and assault) goes home today, two weeks ahead (English and Spanish), with the outline and the opt-out route.

goal: After the week between lessons, the teacher models on one case how to judge an advocacy's effect and a decision's results; then teams judge whether the advocacy made health better (what changed, how we know, what next) and how the decision to run it worked out, with a character case beside it.
note: Retrieval task: grade 7 options at wider levels (unit 16), and SEL unit 13's think-ahead (SEL first). Family note for sensitive unit 29 (suicide: warning signs and help) goes home today, two weeks ahead (English and Spanish), with the outline and the opt-out route.

goal: End-of-unit check: the revised piece scored on the steps, the delivery record and one unseen case with two prompts: did the advocacy make health better and how we know; how the decision to run it worked out for the team and others.
note: End-of-unit assessment: two or three unseen scenarios read alone or aloud on request, the steps written for the character, one facts-in-use item per unit fact, one valuing item scored on whether the reason uses a unit fact; no cards; met, partly or not yet. Self-check 2 after the check.

goal: Healthy and unhealthy relationship signs, coercion, sexual assault named factually, consent, and where to get help; never blame.
